edges.description: Disordered atrial electrical activity produces the arrhythmia phenotype clinically recognized as an irregular pulse.
Atrial fibrillation-related rhythm disturbance commonly manifests as palpitations.
intermediate_mechanisms: symptomatic perception of irregular atrial rhythm

edges.description: AF-related rhythm and hemodynamic disturbance can produce dyspnea.
intermediate_mechanisms: impaired atrial contribution to cardiac output

edges.description: AF symptom burden includes fatigue, often alongside dyspnea and intermittent symptoms.
Atrial thrombus formation creates risk for embolic stroke, which is the main target of anticoagulation.
Microbial TMA is absorbed and delivered to the liver for oxidation.
FMO3 oxidation of TMA yields the circulating metabolite TMAO.
TMAO, structurally similar to acetylcholine, inhibits the cardiac M2 muscarinic receptor.
A choline diet drives left atrial dilation, contributing structural AF substrate in parallel to the autonomic arm.
M2R inhibition disrupts parasympathetic (vagal) cardiac control.
The high-TMAO state is associated with slower conduction velocity and APD80/wavelength shortening, which may lower the reentry threshold and feed electrical remodeling that sustains AF.

nodes.description: Rapid atrial rates cause shortening of atrial refractory period and loss of rate adaptation, promoting AF maintenance. AF begets AF.

evidence.reference_title: Modulation of NOX2 causes obesity-mediated atrial fibrillation.
evidence.snippet: NOX2 inhibition normalized atrial action potential duration and abrogated obesity-mediated ion channel remodeling with reduced AF burden.

nodes.description: Atrial fibrosis and dilation create substrate for AF maintenance. Fibrosis disrupts normal conduction and creates reentrant circuits.

evidence.snippet: Human cAMP response element modulator isoform IbΔC-X transgenic mice (CREM-IbΔC-X), a spontaneous mouse model of AF, supplemented with a TMAO diet developed AF sooner.

nodes.description: Gut bacteria transform dietary choline to trimethylamine (TMA) through the CutC/D pathway. Iodomethylcholine (IMC) inhibits this microbial choline-to-TMA(O) transformation.

evidence.reference_title: Gut microbial trimethylamine N-oxide generation promotes risk of atrial fibrillation via muscarinic receptor-mediated autonomic dysfunction
evidence.snippet: Cecal metagenomic analyses showed that choline supplementation induced changes in microbial communities associated with AF, while many of these changes were attenuated by IMC.

nodes.description: Iodomethylcholine (IMC), a gut-restricted CutC/D choline-TMA lyase inhibitor, suppresses microbial choline-to-TMA(O) transformation, reduces circulating TMAO, and delays choline-induced AF onset in mice. It is an investigational AF-prevention strategy, not yet a human therapy.
